channel.title: The Retreat Register — Updates
channel.description: Verification progress from The Retreat Register, published with real numbers: coverage snapshots, data findings, and what gets cut from the register and why.

item.title: Glamping or Cabins? Choose the Right Lodging for Your Group Retreat
item.description: Canvas tents and cabins can sit on the same property and suit very different groups. A side-by-side look at weather, bathrooms, sleep, and working space.

item.title: How to Host a Silent Retreat: Choose a Venue That Can Hold the Quiet
item.description: A loud, shared, or conversation-centered venue works against a silent retreat. The property checks that matter before a teacher or organizer books.

item.title: Types of Retreats: Match the Format to the Goal Before You Search
item.description: Corporate, wellness, silent, creative, faith-based, and family retreats ask different things of a venue. A guide to the main formats and what to check for each.

item.title: Define a Corporate Retreat Before You Search for Venues
item.description: A corporate retreat takes a team away from the office, usually overnight, for focused work. A plain definition, and how the goal shapes the venue search.

item.title: How to Negotiate a Retreat Venue Quote in One Polite Email
item.description: A venue quote has more parts than the rate. The terms worth asking about, how to put them in one written request, and how to keep the tone friendly.

item.title: How to Check a Venue Booking Before You Send a Deposit
item.description: Look-alike venue listings exist, and a deposit is hard to get back. The desk checks that take minutes, and the payment habits that protect the group.

item.title: How to Ask to Move a Retreat Date and Put the Terms in Writing
item.description: A date change is a different request from a cancellation. How to ask for one, and what to get in writing.

item.title: Retreat Cancellation Clauses: Read the Date-Based Charges Before You Sign
item.description: Some venue contracts charge more to cancel as the date gets closer. How a sliding scale works and which terms are worth asking about.

item.title: The Food and Beverage Minimum: Know What Your Group Must Spend
item.description: A food and beverage minimum is the least a group agrees to spend on catering. What counts toward it, what does not, and what happens if the group falls short.

item.title: The Room Block Cutoff Date: Plan Around When Rooms May Leave the Block
item.description: A cutoff clause states when unbooked rooms in a group block may return to general inventory. How to ask about the date, and what to do before it.

item.title: Room Blocks Explained: Learn the Terms Before You Reserve Group Rooms
item.description: A room block holds rooms for a group under one contract. How the block, the pickup, and the attrition terms fit together.

item.title: Liability Waivers for Retreats: Decide What Guests Sign and When
item.description: Hikes, cold plunges, horses, and ropes courses can raise the waiver question. Who writes it, who collects it, and when guests should see it.

item.title: The Indemnification Clause: Find Out Who Pays When Something Goes Wrong
item.description: One paragraph in a venue contract deals with who bears the cost of an accident or a claim. How to read it, and the questions to bring to an attorney.

item.title: Retreat Liability Insurance: Ask Who Covers the Facilitators and Vendors You Bring
item.description: A retreat may bring in an outside teacher, guide, or caterer. The written questions that show whose insurance applies to them, before the contract is signed.

item.title: The One-Day Retreat: When Skipping the Overnight Is Right
item.description: Sometimes eight focused hours beat two logistics-heavy nights. The honest test for going overnight-free.

item.title: Lake, Mountain, or Desert: Match the Setting to the Retreat's Job
item.description: Setting is a tool - water calms, elevation isolates, desert strips distraction. Pick by agenda, not postcard.

item.title: Retreat House, Retreat Center, or Lodge? Pick the Category First
item.description: The three venue categories serve different group sizes and service levels. Choosing the category first cuts the search in half.

item.title: How Nonprofits Find Retreat Venues That Fit Tight Budgets
item.description: Off-peak dates, simple lodging tiers, and venues whose mission matches - a search strategy, not a discount hunt.

item.title: Shipping Materials to a Venue: Confirm Receiving First
item.description: Boxes arrive before planners do. Receiving policy, storage, and labeling conventions prevent the missing-box scramble.

item.title: Winter Retreats: Settle the Snow Questions Before You Book
item.description: Plowing, road access, heating capacity, and weather cancellation terms - the homework that makes off-season booking safe.
